weeks.headline: Wind should pick up on Tuesday 17 November as rain-bearing systems cross Britain, with gusts of 38-43 mph at the coastal sites we track. By Friday 20 November it falls light almost everywhere, with gusts of only 9-15 mph, so gas is likely to carry more of the load into a cold end to the week. Beyond Thursday, confidence drops.
weeks.summary: A windy Tuesday, a still and frosty Friday, and a less certain weekend.

days.outlook: Windiest day of the week; rain reaches the south.

days.offshore_note: Gusts 26-34 mph; hourly speeds not available
days.outlook: Wind easing; frost in places overnight.
Output fades as the wind drops; cold.

days.offshore_note: Gusts only 9-15 mph at every site

weeks.table_note: Ratings are based on Met Office coastal and town forecasts, which understate wind at turbine hub height. Roughly: under 10 mph low output, 10-20 mph moderate, over 20 mph strong. Confidence falls after Thursday; ranges for Wednesday to Saturday were not available for most sites, so those days rely on gusts.

buyers.label: High-wind periods
buyers.text: Tuesday is the likeliest day for stronger wind output, which tends to soften day-ahead prices. If output is concentrated in Scotland and the North Sea, transmission constraints and some curtailment are possible. The forecast gusts do not point to widespread storm cut-outs.

buyers.label: Low-wind risk
buyers.text: Friday looks the stillest, with gusts of 9-15 mph at every site. Gas is likely to fill the gap, which tends to firm day-ahead and evening-peak prices, especially if it is cold.

buyers.label: Demand
buyers.text: Overnight frost is possible on Wednesday and Thursday (Cambridge and Barrow forecast down to -1°C), with daytime highs of only 6-9°C. That supports heating demand just as wind falls away.

buyers.label: For buyers
buyers.text: Customers on flexible or index-linked contracts are more exposed to day-to-day swings than those on fixed prices. Forecasts beyond Thursday are less reliable, so treat the later part of the week as a range, not a call.

areas.title: Offshore wind (North Sea and Irish Sea)
areas.text: The east coast sees its best winds on Tuesday: Bridlington (Hornsea and Dogger Bank) 7-17 mph with gusts of 39, and Lowestoft (East Anglia offshore) 8-18 mph with gusts of 43. Dunbar (Seagreen, Neart na Gaoithe) has 9-18 mph and gusts of 38. At Barrow-in-Furness (Walney, West of Duddon Sands) the Irish Sea is similar, at 8-19 mph. All of this is below the roughly 55 mph gust level where storm cut-outs become a concern. Winds ease from Wednesday and are light by Friday.

areas.title: Scotland onshore wind and hydro
areas.text: Wick (Moray Firth and Highlands) is moderate on Monday, with gusts of 30-35 mph through Wednesday. The shipping forecast had Cromarty, Forth and Tyne at force 4 to 6, occasionally 7, with gales further north. Only light rain is forecast in the Highlands, so no clear hydro boost.

areas.title: Wales and northern England
areas.text: The mid Wales forecast (Llandrindod Wells) was out of date, so there is no usable Welsh forecast this week. Barrow and Bridlington show the coastal pattern: Tuesday the windiest, then easing.

areas.title: Solar (south and east England)
areas.text: Cambridge is mostly cloudy early in the week, with light rain on Tuesday and sleet showers on Thursday. Winter solar is modest at best; Friday and Saturday bring sunny intervals, the best of the week.

watch.text: Elexon's national wind forecast at the start of the week. Its peak forecasts for 14 and 15 November were about 15 GW, and the window to Tuesday is not yet covered.
The windiest day, with rain moving into the south and possible hill snow. Watch for any Met Office warnings; none were listed at the time of writing.
The lightest winds of the week. Watch the evening peak and gas-fired output.
The Met Office expects changeable weather with Atlantic lows: strong winds possible at times, milder air in the south and sharp frosts in the north.

weeks.caveats: The Met Office page for Llandrindod Wells was stale (dates from October) and was discarded. The Elexon WINDFOR dataset was also stale (published 26 October) and was not used. The Met Office long-range forecast page could not be retrieved. The location forecasts were missing hourly wind speeds for Wednesday onwards, so gusts are used for those days. Forecasts were read on Saturday 14 November.
